ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a human reviewer with a copy of the complete chat (F8-F10) and the GPS segment trace (F3): confirm with route/road-name data whether the 21:58-22:05 driven path was Tampines Avenue 7 as consented; if it was not, apply refund_partial of $3.00 to the rider's voucher (NS-7).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a route_deviation dispute on a metered RydeTAXI trip, so any unexempt extra kilometre feeds the meter and is refundable under RD-2, while a segment excused by the rider's prior consent is not a detour at all under RD-5 [F3][F4][RD-2][RD-5]. The trace settles two elements: an off-route segment exists (RD-1 satisfied, ✓) [F3][RD-1], and no RD-4(a) incident on the replaced stretch was recorded, with speed bands being corroborative only under RD-4(b) [F12][F15][F16][RD-4]. The only live question is RD-5 consent scope for that segment and it changes the amount, so it governs the outcome [F3][RD-5].

On RD-5 the record shows a genuine rider message sent before the segment: the driver asked "can I go round via Tampines Avenue 7?" at 21:55 and the rider replied "可以，走 Tampines Avenue 7 吧。" at 21:56, ahead of the 21:58 segment start; the chat is complete and every message timestamped, so the timing is fixed without the driver's post-trip statement, which has no consent value [F8][F9][F10][F3][F11][RD-5]. Read in context this is neither a general "take whichever way is faster" authorisation nor an undetermined scope: it is a specific named-road consent, so it covers driving on Tampines Avenue 7 only [F8][F9][RD-5].

RD-5 then requires the record to tie the driven segment to that named road — a stop on it, a message placing the car on it, or a road name in a fact — and timing alone is not enough (G13) [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. No fact in the table names the road actually driven, and the segment as measured strays up to 1209 m off the optimal route over 4.04 km where the optimal stretch is 1.90 km; nothing places the car on Tampines Avenue 7 or rules it out [F1][F3][RD-5]. On this record the segment's exemption status cannot be settled: it is undetermined, not "counts", and because this finding changes the amount I cannot enter a refund (or a no_action) myself [F3][F4][RD-5].

The amount that would follow if the segment were not exempt is computed from the fare record's own rate, distance fare ÷ distance km = $28.28 ÷ 20.06 km = $1.4098/km, applied to the segment's extra 2.13 km: 2.13 × $1.4098 = $3.00; the remainder of the billed 2.58 km / $3.64 excess is corridor and map-matching mileage that RD-2 does not refund [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. No flag_account attaches: the driver's 90-day record shows 0 upheld route disputes, so RD-6's "repeated" threshold is not met, and neither advocate maintained the request [F18][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the chat (F8, F9), the driver's statement (F11) and the complaint — a jam query, a route agreement and a fare/route-uncertainty complaint; no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation basis, but the evidence insufficiency sends the case to a person anyway [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1].
